    - Hm. Those boots you've got on. Who made those? Doesn't matter. They'll be done in two winters. Mine'd see you buried.
    - You again. Boy's sweeping my step again. Hm. Step's never been so clean. Don't tell him I said so.
    - *Player*. Howler hide's curing in the back. Good thick stuff. Kite's next pair will outlast Kite's grandchildren. As it should.
    - Well? Buying, or wearing out my floor?
        - *Choice:* Let me see your boots.
        - *Choice:* What makes a rooftop boot?
        - *Choice:* Who taught you?
        - *Choice:* Why not take an apprentice?
        - *Choice:* Nothing.
    - Try them on proper. Both feet. Walk to the door and back. If it pinches, say so. I won't sell a boot that pinches.
    - Soft sole, thin enough to feel a slate shift, tough enough to take a gutter edge. Stitched round, not nailed: nails ring on a roof and slip on a wet one. I worked it out myself, my first years on my own. Nobody else had bothered.
    - Made the first pair for Kite's grandmother, when I was young and she was fast. Then Kite's mother. Then Kite, four years back. Three generations of runners in my soles. Kite's times are on the back of that door. Kite keeps beating them. Good.
    - Henrike Tull. Walker's daughter. Never joined a guild, never wanted to. Took me on at fourteen and said nothing kind to me for ten years. Left me the shop and the lasts when she died. Best teacher a man ever had.
    - Want one. Haven't found one. They come in, I look at their hands. Wrong sort, every one. Too quick, too soft, too proud. That Selsior boy's asked three times. Wrong sort of hands. Probably.
    - Still looking. Hm. The Selsior boy made a sheath for my awl out of a scrap I'd have thrown away. Straight stitches. Hm. Still the wrong sort of hands. Probably. Ask me next season.
    - Mind the step. It's clean.
